questions.stem: Root hair cells have long, thin extensions into the soil. How does this shape help with water absorption?

options.text: It helps the root grip the soil more firmly
It greatly increases the surface area in contact with soil water, increasing the rate of osmosis
It allows the root to reach deeper into the soil
It stores more water inside the cell

questions.explanation: The long, thin root hair projections massively increase the surface area of the root in contact with the thin film of water surrounding soil particles. This allows much more water to be absorbed by osmosis at any one time than if the root surface were smooth. A single root hair cell can increase surface area by up to 100 times.

questions.stem: Water moves from the soil into root hair cells by osmosis. What drives this movement?

options.text: Soil water is at higher pressure than the root cell
The root cell sap has a higher solute concentration (lower water potential) than the dilute soil water, so water moves in by osmosis
Active transport pumps water into the cell
Gravity pulls water downward into the roots

questions.explanation: Root hair cells contain dissolved sugars, minerals, and other solutes, giving them a lower water potential than the relatively dilute soil water. Water moves by osmosis from the higher water potential in the soil to the lower water potential inside the root hair cell, across the partially permeable cell membrane.

questions.stem: Once inside the root, water moves across the cortex to the xylem. It can travel via the apoplast pathway (through cell walls) or the symplast pathway (through cytoplasm via plasmodesmata). At the endodermis, the Casparian strip forces water into the symplast pathway. Why?

options.text: The Casparian strip provides energy for water movement
The Casparian strip is a waterproof band of suberin that blocks the apoplast route, forcing water through living cell membranes where its passage can be controlled
The Casparian strip absorbs minerals from the water
The Casparian strip speeds up water flow

questions.explanation: The Casparian strip is a band of waterproof suberin in the endodermis cell walls. It blocks water from continuing through the apoplast (cell wall) pathway, forcing it through the cell membranes and cytoplasm (symplast). This gives the plant control over which dissolved substances enter the xylem, acting as a selective barrier.

questions.stem: Mineral ions (such as nitrate and magnesium) are present in very low concentrations in soil water. How do root hair cells absorb these minerals?

options.text: By osmosis, along with the water
By diffusion down the concentration gradient
By active transport, using energy from respiration to move minerals against the concentration gradient
Minerals enter through the cell wall passively

questions.explanation: The concentration of mineral ions inside root cells is typically higher than in the dilute soil solution, so minerals cannot enter by diffusion (which requires movement from high to low concentration). Instead, root hair cells use active transport, powered by ATP from aerobic respiration, to absorb mineral ions against the concentration gradient.

questions.stem: If soil becomes waterlogged (flooded), plants may wilt and show signs of mineral deficiency despite plenty of water being available. What causes this?

options.text: Waterlogged soil contains too many minerals, which are toxic
Waterlogged soil lacks oxygen for aerobic respiration, so root cells cannot produce ATP for active transport of minerals
Water pressure in the soil pushes minerals away from roots
The roots grow too quickly in waterlogged conditions

questions.explanation: Waterlogged soil has very little oxygen because water fills the air spaces between soil particles. Root cells need oxygen for aerobic respiration to produce ATP. Without ATP, active transport of mineral ions stops. Additionally, the lack of oxygen can damage root cells directly. Some root cells may die, further reducing the plant's ability to absorb water and minerals.
